Negative Binomial, Cox and Multinomial Fits

extended_families.Rd

Additional likelihood families using existing ridge kernels and family-specific IRLS. See the separate mathematical help pages for each family.

Details

Use L0glm.fit(X,y,family=mgcv::nb()) for estimated-shape NB, family=mgcv::nb(theta=2) for fixed shape, or family=mgcv::nb(theta=-2) to estimate from a starting shape of 2. Each NB channel has its own shape parameter; scale dispersion is one. Positive weights are prior/case weights. Offsets are included in the link.

Use family=mgcv::cox.ph() with right-censored survival::Surv(time,status) or an ordinary two-column time/status matrix. Status belongs in the response, not in weights. Cox uses weighted Breslow ties, partial likelihood, and no intercept. Delayed entry, strata, time-varying predictors, multiple states and other tie methods are not implemented. Survival predictions use an estimated Breslow baseline hazard.

Use family=mgcv::multinom(K=2) for three categories, supplied as a factor or three-column integer count matrix. All K+1 category coefficients are returned in centered log-ratio (CLR) coordinates: every coefficient row sums to zero. A free intercept is added by default. Starts, offsets and prior means also have K+1 columns and are centered across categories. Common shifts have no effect on probabilities. All-zero starting rows exclude predictors before CLR centering; individual category zeroes in other rows remain eligible. Scalar start=1 centers to zero while keeping all rows eligible; start=0 fits only mandatory terms. Intercepts and always.include rows remain eligible even with zero starts. Eligible zero starts receive one weak-ridge IRLS step before adaptive weighting. Returned sparse coefficients retain their original predictor and category dimensions, including excluded zero rows. Nonnegative=TRUE is ignored with a warning. The model and output stay in CLR; K orthonormal contrast coordinates are used only to solve nonsingular linear systems efficiently.

prior.mean supplies ridge-penalty centers in original input coefficient units: a scalar, length-\(p\) vector, or \(p\) by \(m\) matrix, with any added intercept included in \(p\). NB uses one column per response channel; Cox uses one column, no intercept, and centers log-relative-hazard coefficients rather than the baseline hazard. NB shape is not a prior target. Multinomial uses all K+1 category columns and centers each target row to CLR; scalar or vector targets shared across categories become zero. NULL also uses zero targets. A nonzero target cannot override an excluded starting coefficient or multinomial row, which remains zero in the full-size sparse output. Mandatory terms remain unpenalized. Adaptive weights and support counts still use coefficients relative to zero, rather than deviations from the targets. Special-family relaxed refits remove the ridge penalty on retained support, so the targets no longer exert shrinkage during that refit.

Multinomial uses coupled block IRLS with the exact class covariance. IRLS for logistic models is algebraically equivalent to a Newton/Fisher-scoring step, expressed as weighted least squares. It is not independent binomial fitting. The alternative control.family=list(multinomial="bound") uses a diagonal upper curvature bound on the zero-sum plane inspired by Krishnapuram et al.; their paper uses an L1 penalty, while the adaptive L0 extension here is separate.

Grouped selection penalizes a predictor row if any channel or CLR category coefficient is nonzero. Its adaptive ridge weights are shared across a row. NB ungrouped selection counts individual channel coefficients. Multinomial ungrouped selection counts individual CLR entries, with zero-sum rows; it still fits the joint multinomial likelihood. Grouped multinomial selection instead counts active rows using a category-invariant CLR row norm. Its parameter-count IC charges K free directions per active row. Cox has one coefficient per predictor, so grouped and ungrouped selection coincide.

For normalized working coefficients \(b\), gamma (default two) sets the unsmoothed adaptive weights: \(D_{jc}=\lambda/(4\|b_j\|_2^\gamma)\) for grouped multichannel NB and multinomial models, and \(D_{jc}=\lambda/(4|b_{jc}|^\gamma)\) for ungrouped or single-channel fits, including Cox. Scale dispersion is one. thresh (default 1e-5) acts on row norms for grouped selection, removing whole rows, and on individual magnitudes within each response/category column for ungrouped or single-channel selection. The relative cutoff is thresh times the corresponding largest selectable magnitude; an absolute 1e-20 cutoff also applies. Mandatory terms are excluded from these maxima and never thresholded. Retained grouped rows do not receive individual-entry hard cutoffs. Multinomial surviving entries are recentered within their allowed category set, keeping removed entries zero; rows with fewer than two allowed entries are zero. Cutoffs apply only in selection passes with positive lambda. thresh=0 retains the absolute cutoff, and thresh does not smooth adaptive weights.

With relaxed=TRUE, special families refit using lambda=0 without hard thresholding. Grouped refits admit all eligible entries in retained rows; ungrouped refits admit only entries nonzero at the end of selection. A grouped multinomial refit can recover category entries within a retained row, whereas an ungrouped refit holds unselected CLR entries at zero. Both retain zero-sum rows: s admitted category entries give s-1 free directions. No new predictor rows enter the refit. Starting exclusions remain binding, and mandatory terms remain eligible and unpenalized. Estimated NB shapes continue to be updated. Sparse outputs retain all original coefficient dimensions. Relaxed fitting is enabled by default for grouped multichannel NB and all grouped multinomial responses, but not for Cox, ungrouped fits or single-channel NB. Each pass uses maxit; group.maxit is unused. Tuning applies refits to each candidate and within CV training folds before scoring; pilot fits are unrelaxed. The reported L0 objective is a target for a heuristic, not a global certificate. There is no reference category in multinomial fitting or selection.

L0glm.metrics reports exact family likelihoods when mu_floor=0, the family deviance, the target L0 objective, row GIC and parameter-count ICs. Object metrics and logLik use exact likelihoods. External NB scoring defaults to a mean floor of 1e-8. Cox deviance is -2 times partial log likelihood, not an ordinary saturated-model deviance. Grouped IC tuning uses row counts; metrics$tuning_score is the actual selection score, while gic retains the parameter-count definition. CV returns full-data best and one-SE fits. NB CV keeps theta fixed at its training estimate when scoring validation data. Cox CV uses full-minus-training partial likelihood, preserving full risk sets.

These loops are serial. Cox caches risk sets and uses matrix-free PCG for large, wide or sparse unrestricted Eigen systems, retaining LLT for small dense active systems. Its weak-ridge initializer is also matrix-free. Direct Cox and block multinomial curvature systems are guarded by control.family$max.working. Wide direct systems use whitening and the existing Woodbury ridge route. The bound option changes curvature, not the definition of the likelihood. No new compiled code or dependency imports are required; the mgcv constructors are optional and reference packages are listed in Suggests.

References

Krishnapuram, B., Carin, L., Figueiredo, M. A. T. and Hartemink, A. J. (2005). Sparse multinomial logistic regression: Fast algorithms and generalization bounds. IEEE TPAMI 27(6), 957–968.

Verweij, P. J. M. and van Houwelingen, H. C. (1993). Cross-validation in survival analysis. Statistics in Medicine 12, 2305–2314.
